stem: An adult has decreased alertness after a nontraumatic medical event but is breathing normally and does not require CPR. Which position is reasonable while awaiting further care?

options.A: Side-lying recovery position with continued monitoring
options.B: Prone with the face against the floor
options.D: Trendelenburg position for every cause of altered alertness

rationale: Current AHA/Red Cross first-aid guidance states that a person with decreased alertness from a nontraumatic cause who is breathing normally may reasonably be placed in a side-lying recovery position. Ongoing monitoring is important because recognition of respiratory arrest can be delayed in this position.
educational_objective: Use the recovery position appropriately for a nontraumatic, decreased-alertness client who is breathing normally.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American Red Cross
source_locator: Recovery position: decreased alertness, nontraumatic cause, normal breathing; side-lying reasonable; continue monitoring
source_claim_supported: For nontraumatic decreased alertness with normal breathing, side-lying recovery position is reasonable with continued monitoring.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
correction_summary: Reclassified from Basic Care and Comfort to Physiological Adaptation and added the guideline's normal-breathing/nontraumatic qualifiers plus monitoring caveat.
